A turbine airfoil includes a generally hollow airfoil body having an internal cooling structure defined by adjacent partition walls. Positioned between these partition walls is a flow displacement element configured to influence and divide the internal cooling flow.

The flow displacement element includes an elongated main body that extends generally in a radial direction within the airfoil. The main body is connected to the pressure side and the suction side of the airfoil by connector ribs, which support the element and help define internal cooling passages.

On opposite chordal sides of the flow displacement element, adjacent radial flow passes are formed. These radial flow passes have cross-sections that are symmetrically opposed to one another, thereby creating complementary flow channels on either side of the flow displacement element.

During operation, cooling fluid flows through the adjacent radial flow passes in opposite radial directions. For example, cooling fluid may travel radially outward through one flow pass and radially inward through the adjacent flow pass. The flow passes are fluidly connected in series by a chordal passage, allowing the cooling fluid to turn from one radial flow pass into the next.

Together, the radial flow passes and the chordal passage form a serpentine cooling path within the hollow airfoil body. This serpentine path enhances internal cooling effectiveness by directing the cooling fluid through multiple passes along the airfoil before it exits or continues to additional cooling features.

A turbine airfoil includes an internal cooling arrangement designed to improve the distribution and management of cooling fluid within the airfoil body. The airfoil has an internal cavity divided by a plurality of partition walls that extend generally in a radial direction. Within this cavity, an internal flow displacement element is positioned between adjacent partition walls. The flow displacement element includes connector ribs that cooperate with the partition walls to define paired radial cooling passages located on opposite chordal sides of the element.

Each pair of passages includes a first radial passage on one chordal side of the flow displacement element and a second radial passage on the opposite chordal side. Cooling fluid flows through these opposed passages in opposite radial directions. For example, cooling fluid may travel radially outward through one passage and radially inward through the corresponding passage on the other side. The passages are connected to one another by chordwise or chordal passages, allowing the cooling fluid to turn between the opposed radial passages.

Together, the radial passages and chordal connecting passages form a serpentine cooling path within the turbine airfoil. This serpentine flow path increases the effective cooling length, promotes better heat transfer from the airfoil walls to the cooling fluid, and helps regulate the movement of cooling fluid through the interior of the airfoil. By guiding the cooling fluid through controlled, alternating radial flow directions, the arrangement improves internal cooling efficiency and helps maintain acceptable airfoil temperatures during turbine operation.

The use of the internal flow displacement element and connector ribs also helps organize the internal flow structure without requiring an excessive number of separate walls or complex cast features. As a result, the cooling system can provide enhanced thermal performance while maintaining structural integrity and manufacturability of the turbine airfoil. This configuration is particularly useful in high-temperature turbine environments, where effective internal cooling is necessary to protect the airfoil from thermal damage and to extend component service life.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps us identify a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, when we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that both the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” seems simple, it gives sentences clarity and precision. It can point to something already mentioned, such as “I saw a dog. The dog was friendly.” It can also refer to something unique, like “the sun,” “the moon,” or “the world.” Without this small word, many sentences would feel incomplete or unclear.

The word “the” also shows how powerful language can be. Even the shortest words can carry meaning, create context, and guide understanding. In everyday speech and writing, “the” helps connect ideas and make communication smoother.

In short, “the” may be tiny, but it is essential. It reminds us that even the simplest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a turbine airfoil with an internal flow displacement element, adjacent partition walls, connector ribs, and opposed radial cooling passages forming a serpentine cooling path.
counterfactuals.output: A turbine airfoil includes an airfoil body having pressure and suction sidewalls extending radially between a root and a tip and defining an internal cooling cavity. A flow displacement element is disposed within the internal cooling cavity and is spaced from the sidewalls to form cooling flow passages. A plurality of partition walls extend adjacent to the flow displacement element to subdivide the cooling cavity, and connector ribs couple the flow displacement element to one or more of the partition walls and/or sidewalls to provide structural support and to guide coolant flow. Opposed radial cooling passages are defined on opposite sides of the flow displacement element and are fluidly connected at radial ends to form a serpentine cooling path through the airfoil. The serpentine cooling path directs cooling fluid alternately in radially outward and radially inward directions to increase coolant residence time and convective heat transfer while maintaining airfoil structural integrity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention described in this patent claim: a hollow turbine airfoil body has pressure and suction sides, internal partition walls, a radial elongated displacement body connected by ribs, and cooling fluid passages that reverse direction through chordal passages near the end faces.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a cooled hollow turbine airfoil, such as a turbine blade or vane, designed to improve internal cooling efficiency.

It has:

- A hollow airfoil body with pressure and suction side walls.
- Internal partition walls that divide the hollow interior into cooling passages.
- A radially elongated displacement body inside the airfoil, connected to the surrounding walls by ribs.
- Cooling fluid passages that guide cooling air radially through the airfoil.
- Near the end faces of the airfoil, chordwise passages connect the radial passages so the cooling fluid reverses direction and continues through another passage.

In essence, the design creates a multi-pass cooling circuit inside the turbine airfoil. The displacement body and ribs shape and control the cooling flow, while the end-region chordal passages turn the flow around. This helps distribute cooling air more effectively through the blade or vane, especially near thermally stressed regions, improving durability and cooling performance.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical description of a gas turbine blade cooling arrangement where a central insert between partition walls creates symmetric adjacent radial flow passes connected in series to form serpentine cooling circuits.
counterfactuals.output: A gas turbine blade cooling arrangement includes an internal cavity divided by generally radial partition walls and a central insert positioned between the partition walls. The insert cooperates with the adjacent partition walls to define two substantially symmetric radial cooling flow passes on opposite sides of the insert. The radial passes are fluidly connected in series by turn regions at alternating ends of the blade, thereby forming one or more serpentine cooling circuits within the blade airfoil. Cooling air flows successively through the adjacent passes, reversing direction at each turn, to provide distributed internal convective cooling of the blade while maintaining balanced flow distribution on both sides of the insert.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in the style of a patent publication, a generally hollow turbine airfoil having a flow displacement element between adjacent internal walls, connector ribs to pressure and suction sides, and opposite-direction radial cooling passes linked by chordal passages.
counterfactuals.output:
A turbine airfoil is provided for use in a gas turbine engine, the airfoil including an outer wall defining a generally hollow interior. The outer wall includes a pressure side wall and an opposed suction side wall extending generally chordwise between a leading edge region and a trailing edge region and generally radially between a root and a tip.

Within the hollow interior, a plurality of internal walls define a cooling circuit. At least two adjacent internal walls are spaced apart to form a generally radial cooling passage therebetween. A flow displacement element is disposed between the adjacent internal walls and extends at least partially in the radial direction. The flow displacement element is spaced from the adjacent internal walls so as to divide or constrict coolant flow within the radial passage, thereby increasing local coolant velocity, promoting turbulence, and improving heat transfer to the internal walls.

The flow displacement element is mechanically supported by a plurality of connector ribs. At least one connector rib extends from the flow displacement element toward, and is joined with, the pressure side wall. At least one additional connector rib extends from the flow displacement element toward, and is joined with, the suction side wall. The connector ribs may be arranged at discrete radial locations and may extend generally chordwise, laterally, or obliquely relative to the radial direction. The connector ribs provide structural support for the flow displacement element while also functioning as heat transfer features within the cooling circuit.

The internal walls cooperate to define a serpentine cooling arrangement including at least a first radial cooling pass and a second radial cooling pass. The first radial cooling pass is configured to direct cooling fluid in a first radial direction, and the second radial cooling pass is configured to direct cooling fluid in a second radial direction opposite the first radial direction. For example, the first radial cooling pass may convey coolant radially outwardly toward the airfoil tip, while the second radial cooling pass conveys coolant radially inwardly toward the root, or vice versa.

The first and second radial cooling passes are fluidly connected by one or more chordal passages extending generally in the chordwise direction within the airfoil. The chordal passages may be positioned near a radially outer turn region, a radially inner turn region, or at an intermediate radial location. Each chordal passage permits coolant to turn from one radial pass into an adjacent radial pass, thereby forming a multi-pass cooling circuit within the generally hollow airfoil.

In one embodiment, the flow displacement element is positioned in one of the radial cooling passes between adjacent internal walls that separate the radial pass from neighboring cooling passages. The displacement element may have an elongate body with rounded, tapered, or airfoil-shaped surfaces to reduce pressure loss while maintaining enhanced convective cooling. The connector ribs may be integrally cast with the pressure side wall, suction side wall, internal walls, and flow displacement element.

During operation, cooling air supplied to the hollow interior flows through the radial cooling passes and the chordal passages. As the cooling air passes around the flow displacement element and connector ribs, the available flow area is locally reduced and the coolant is redirected toward heated internal surfaces of the pressure and suction side walls. The arrangement provides improved internal cooling effectiveness while maintaining structural integrity of the airfoil under centrifugal, thermal, and gas loading conditions.
